chunks: And it was narrated from Al-Kāhilī that he said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: My wife and my sister—who is the wife of Muḥammad ibn Mārid—go out to mourning gatherings, so I forbid them. Then they said to me: If it is haram, we will desist from it; but if it is not haram, then why do you prevent us, such that people refrain from fulfilling our rights?
So he عليه السلام said: About rights you ask me? My father عليه السلام used to send my mother and Umm Farwah to fulfill the rights of the people of al-Madīnah.

key_terms.الْحُقُوقِ: rights and obligations due to people
key_terms.الْمَآتِمِ: mourning gatherings or assemblies of grief
key_terms.حُقُوقِنَا: our due rights owed by others in social relations

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for women to attend mourning gatherings to fulfill social rights in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses whether women may go out to mourning gatherings when doing so is connected to the fulfillment of social rights. Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام responds by citing the practice of his father عليه السلام, indicating that women’s participation in such social duties was recognized and not treated as haram in this context.
